##### FFRCISTG

To fully characterize the NPSEM specified above using observed data, we would need to estimate nine functions using one observation of the nine-dimensional joint distribution that gave rise to the participants’ observations. Recruiting an additional person to the study would not ease this problem; it would add three new equations to the model, and we would end up with a similar problem to the one we began with. We would have to estimate 12 functions using one observation of a 12-dimensional joint distribution.

We can simplify this system of equations by making assumptions that remove edges from the graph, assumptions that leave us with fewer functions to estimate and more observations per function (homogeneity assumptions), and an assumption about the counterfactuals that lets us identify effects.

The finest fully randomized causally interpretable structured tree graph (FFRCISTG) is a causal model of an NPSEM that satisfies (1) no contagion, (2) no interference, (3) identical structural distributions and (4) single-world independence: the one-step-ahead counterfactuals are mutually independent (@def-ffrcistg). No contagion and no interference restrict the graph; identical structural distributions is a statistical assumption; single-world independence is the causal one. Under (1), (2) and (4) the observational units are independent of each other, and under (3) they are also identically distributed. For a single unit this is Robins' FFRCISTG.

**Where the names come from.** The FFRCISTG is due to Robins [-@robins1986]. Richardson and Robins [-@richardson2013] state it relative to a DAG, as the assumption that one-step-ahead counterfactuals are mutually independent: assumption (4) of @def-ffrcistg, written out in @def-single-world. Assumptions (1)–(3) are not part of Robins' definition. We add them so that observational units are independent and identically distributed, which is the setting of this chapter.

The network models later in this appendix are not new kinds of model. The NFFRCISTG (@def-nffrcistg) replaces no interference with homogeneous network interference, and applies single-world independence to the DAG whose nodes are every unit's variables. The RNFFRCISTG (@def-rnffrcitg) generates the network inside the model, with relational equations for its edges, keeps single-world independence, taking each graph generator as a single variable: the network must be independent of the structural counterfactuals, and nothing is assumed about how edges depend on each other. In the BRNFFRCISTG (@def-brnffrcistg) each person's network weights belong to their observational unit, so the network is person-level data and the same assumptions cover it. The DBRNFFRCISTG (@def-dbrnffrcistg) takes each person–place tie, rather than each person's row, as a single variable. The prefixes N, RN, BRN and DBRN are our labels for these combinations, as are the names RNNPSEM (@def-npsem-ne), BRNNPSEM (@def-bipartite-npsem-ie) and DBRNNPSEM (@def-dyadic-npsem). None is standard terminology.
